full_judgment:
Sheikh Hassan Arif J: Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the action of the respondents in depriving the petitioner of his fundamental rights by not delivering petitioner's passport, being No. EA0645991, as per delivery slip (Annexure-C), should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, and as to why the respondents should not be directed to deliver petitioner's passport immediately. 

 6. Mr Khandker Mahbub Hossain, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner, at the outset of the hearing, has drawn this Court's attention to the delivery slip as issued in favour of the petitioner by the passport authority, as annexed to the writ petition as Annexure-C. Learned advocate submits that it is apparent from the said delivery slip that the petitioner applied for the re-issuance of passport on 26-5-2019 and the collection/delivery date of the said passport was 4-6-2019. However, according to him, almost 2 (two) months have elapsed in the meantime, but the petitioner has got no response from the passport authority as regards status of his passport. Further referring to the provisions under Article 5 of the President's Order 1973 (PO 09 of 1973), learned advocate submits that the passport authority is required to conduct enquiry, either by police or somebody else, only in case of issuance of new passport. According to him, since the number of the earlier passport of the petitioner has already been given to the authority, and since all the particulars of the petitioner are lying in the concerned file with the authority, there is no necessity on the part of the authority to wait for the police report for re-issuance of passport in favour of the petitioner. Further drawing this Court's attention to the letter issued by one Assistant Director of Pabna Passport Office dated 27-5-2019 (Annexure-D), learned advocate submits that in the said letter the petitioner was deliberately identified as BNP politician, though the petitioner did not apply for such issuance of passport as a politician, rather he applied as a citizen of this country. Therefore, according to him, identifying the petitioner by this letter as BNP politician is mala-fide and has been done only to deprive the petitioner of his right to obtain passport within the shortest possible time so that the fundamental rights of the petitioner to go abroad and re-enter Bangladesh are violated. Therefore, learned advocate for the petitioner submits that necessary consequential direction should be given by this Court to the concerned authority to re-issue the passport in favour of the petitioner within the shortest possible time. 

 8. It appears from materials on record, in particular Article 36 of our Constitution that it is the fundamental right of every citizen of this Country, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in public interest, that he shall have the right to move freely throughout the Bangladesh and to reside in any place therein and to leave and re-enter Bangladesh. Therefore, it appears that any citizen of this country has been guaranteed fundamental rights by the Constitution to leave this country and to re-enter the country freely subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest. As against this guarantee of fundamental rights, if we examine the materials on record as well as the submissions of the learned advocates, it appears that there is nothing in Articles 5 and 6 of the PO 9 of 1973 which requires enquiry for the purpose of re-issuance of passport. It is very much understandable as to why the legislature has not made such requirement given that the individual applying for re-issuance of passport has already obtained a passport from the passport authority and his particulars are lying with the passport authority in the concerned files. This mandate of law is clearly reflected in the Citizen's Charter as published by the Divisional Passport Authority, Agargaon, Dhaka (Annexure-G to the supplementary affidavit of the petitioner dated 29-8-2019). While Clause 7 of this Citizen's Charter provides for requirement of police report in case of issuance of fresh passport, it does not provide for such requirement under Clause-11 for re-issuance of passport in case of the missing of passports of any citizen. According to this Clause 11 of the said Citizen's Charter, the individual concerned is only required to fill-up a one-page form and deposit certain fees for such re-issuance of passport in his/her favour. He or she is not even required to furnish his attested photograph. This means that, in case of re-issuance of passport, the passport authority does not need to take particulars of the applicant on the ground that the said particulars are already with them. The passport authority does not also need any police enquiry report for such re-issuance as because the same was already obtained when the passport was issued for the first time. 

 9. It appears from the affidavit-in-opposition of respondent No.2 that this respondent has not stated that the delay in re-issuing passport is taking place as because the authority is still waiting for enquiry report. However, it appears from the letter dated 30-7-2019 (Annexure-F that to the petitioner's application) that, the concerned Assistant Director gave such excuse in support of such delay and has even substantiated his such contention relying on Article 5(2) of the Bangladesh Passport Order, 1973, in particular when Article 5(2) of the said Presidential Order does not provide any such requirement of enquiry report for re-issuance of passport. Therefore, whatever may be the political identity of the petitioner, we are of the view that, the first and fore-most identity of the petitioner is that he is a citizen of this country, and like any other citizens of this country, he is entitled to get equal protection of relevant provisions of law (See Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution). While Article 36 of the Constitution has given him guaranteed fundamental rights which is enforceable by this Court, and when he approaches this Court for enforcement such fundamental rights, this Court has obligation to facilitate such enforcement. Therefore, we hold that the concerned authority has in fact violated the fundamental rights of the petitioner to travel beyond Bangladesh and to re-enter Bangladesh subject to the reasonable restrictions of law. No reasonable restriction of law has been referred to by the learned advocate appearing for the passport authority by which the petitioner may be prevented from travelling abroad and/or to re-enter Bangladesh. No relevant restriction of law has also been referred to by the learned advocate for the respondent No. 2 as regards the delay in reissuing such passport in favour of the petitioner. 

 10. Though the petitioner has not pleaded in the writ petition and supplementary-affidavit that he has been victimized for his political identity, it is apparent from the memo dated 27-5-2019, as issued by the Assistant Director of Pabna Passport Office (Annexure-D), that the Passport Authority is not treating the petitioner as an ordinary citizen of this country, rather they are dealing his case separately and discriminatorily by treating him as a “বিএনপি রাজনীতিবিদ (BNP Politician). This being so, we are of the view that the respondent authorities have committed gross illegality not only in depriving the petitioner of his fundamental rights to travel abroad and re-enter Bangladesh as guaranteed under Article 36 of the Constitution, but also in victimizing him for his political identity. 

 12. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. Thus, the actions of the respondents in depriving the petitioner of his fundamental rights by not delivering his passport, being No. EA0645991, as per delivery slip (Annexure-C) is declared to be without lawful authority. Consequently, the respondent authorities, in particular respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4, are directed to re-issue passport in favour of the petitioner within a period of 07(seven) working days from receipt of the copy of this order.
